سَعِيرٌ Lighted, or kindled; or made to burn, burn up, burn brightly or fiercely, blaze, or flame: (K, TA:) of the measure فَعِيلٌ in the sense of the measure مَفْعُولٌ: (TA:) [and thus] similar to دَهِينٌ and صَرِيعٌ; for you say نَارٌ
↓ مَسْعُورَةٌ : (Akh, S:) or نَارٌ سَعِيرٌ signifies fire kindled, or made to burn &c., with other fire. (Lh, TA.) ―
-b2- Also Fire (S, K) itself; (S;) and so ↓ سَاعُورَةٌ and ↓ سَاعُورٌ : (K:) or [so in the TA, but in the K “ and, ”] its flame; (K;) as also ↓ سَاعُورَةٌ and ↓ سَاعُورٌ . (TA.) ＝
-A2- السَّعِيرُ: see what next follows.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
